Question 9

31. Since the initial stage when China Status was engaged in connection with this project, my understanding from Mr. Cheung was that PC&E would be responsible for the posting of notices to inform residents of the shutdown of the respective FH / HR Systems.

32. I would ensure that the notices were provided to PC&E after the FSD acknowledged receipt of SDNs or extension notices, for PC&E’s handling. I do not know who in fact posted the notices or when the notices were posted.

33. For practical and efficiency purposes, at times shutdown notices for several months were prepared and provided to PC&E in advance. This can be seen from Annexure 2.

34. A copy set of all notices provided to PC&E regarding the shutdown of the FH / HR Systems are at Annexure 4.

Question 10.1

35. I did not attend Wang Fuk Court to personally shut down the FH / HR Systems, and I understand that no personnel of China Status did.

36. I understood it was a legal requirement that these systems had to be shut down personally by a registered FSI contractor or under the supervision of a registered FSI contractor.

37. The reason myself or my colleagues did not personally attend to the shutting down of the FH / HR Systems, is because:

(i) I had been informed by Mr. Cheung of PC&E at the commencement of our involvement in this project, that Wang Fuk Court’s building management would handle the physical shutting down of the FH / HR Systems, and that in any event building management would not allow others (which at the time I understood included personnel of China Status) inside their premises; and
